instruction.text: Read the chapter, then answer the reading comprehension questions.

atoms.text: I can’t believe I just got into a fight with Norbert. He attacked me out of nowhere! What was I supposed to do? I had to fight back. The teachers are definitely going to take my side. I mean, he attacked me and anything else would be unfair. Still, I feel a bit panicky, and my stomach has dropped about four escalators below where it usually is.

We all walk into the head teacher’s office: it’s me, Norbert, Mrs Bailey, Mr Radley – the other year five teacher, who is known for being mean – and the head teacher, Mrs Vanderweilen. Norbert and I sit in the chairs in front of Mrs Vanderweilen while Mr Radley and Mrs Bailey stand next to us. I have to say, the office feels pretty full.

Mrs Vanderweilen starts talking, and I have to concentrate. I’m surprised when Norbert admits he started it. His elbows are bleeding, and he has some blood on his lip, which I hadn’t noticed until now. Mrs Vanderweilen talks about how “good young boys behave themselves.” Apparently, we aren’t doing it right. In the end, we are assigned to a few volunteering hours that we have to complete together. Great, more time having to smell Norbert.

After the head teacher is done talking, I start trying to get up to leave, but Mrs Bailey asks me not to. Norbert gets to leave. Unfair. When Norbert is gone, Mrs Bailey turns to me looking really disappointed. She starts asking me uncomfortable questions like: “Do you know why I assigned your seat next to Norbert?”, “Have you ever bothered to ask Norbert about himself?”. My answers are of course “no”. How can I possibly read her mind? With each “no” she shakes her head and looks sad.

Then I get a second assignment. Again, unfair. Mrs Bailey tells me that during our volunteering hours together, I should try to get to know Norbert better. She will be checking in on us, and if I want to stay on her good side, I should try hard to befriend Norbert. The head teacher nods her head, agreeing with Mrs Bailey. Why am I so unlucky, and why is life so unfair? Why does Norbert have to always be my problem?

atoms.a: What do you think the metaphor “My stomach feels about four escalators below where it usually is” means?
b: Jake really needs to use the toilet.
Jake hit his head and thinks the school has escalators.
++Jake is nervous and that makes his stomach feel a bit wonky.

atoms.a: What is the setting of this chapter?

b: ++He is supposed to get to know Norbert better.
He has to write a report about his experience.
He has to continue cleaning for an additional week.

atoms.a: How does Jake feel treated by the adults in the chapter?
